data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The 3-of-26 distribution is not a property of the tests but of the registry's coverage boundary: a test constrains only when the subject's mutation surface overlaps the registry's declared-data schema, and describes whenever the mutation falls in the added-behavior region the registry does not index.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If a surviving mutation changes a declared-data field and still escapes, the registry-boundary explanation is insufficient.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 1/9 compile.py loss is in a registry-indexed code path, the mechanism fails.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If a module with full registry coverage still loses a mutation, the 4/4 to 6/7 pattern is confounded.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the distribution is uniform across guarded and unguarded modules, the boundary claim is falsified.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Ordinarily-guarded modules showed 4/4 to 6/7 because their registry entries enumerate declared data fields, and mutations that change those fields are caught by construction \u2014 the test is a tautological restatement of the registry schema. The compile.py mutation that escaped at 1/9 fell in a code region where no registry entry existed, so the test could only describe the observed behavior rather than derive it from a constraint. The three survivors are all one bug in two costumes: guards checking declared data cannot see added behavior, so the test describes the behavior it observes while appearing to constrain it.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
